I have a daughter. She's 18 months and I remember the 8 month phase very well. You would be astounded at how intelligent they are at that age. Before you have kids you kind of just assume they're mindless little eating, sleeping, and shitting machines - but all they're doing are making connections and learning cause and effect. At that age, they understand that if they smile at you, it will cause you to smile back. If they deliberately drop a toy, they know you'll retrieve it for them.

Not only that, but they have different cries for different needs. You can tell by how your baby is crying if they're overtired, hungry, or uncomfortable.

So imagine being 8 months old. Having a wet diaper is enough to distress you enough to make you cry. After all, being slightly hungry, tired, or uncomfortable is literally the worst thing you've ever experienced. Now imagine the person you love and trust - and you cannot fathom how much an infant loves and trusts you - hears your cries for help and, instead of soothing you, they attack.

Now all of a sudden, the person you love and trust so implicitly that mistrust is a concept outside the real of your experience, attacks you. It would be both indescribable pain and indescribable betray in the context of your experiences.
